description: When people imagine an advanced humanoid robot, they often picture a machine that walks perfectly and never falls. But many robotics researchers are interested in almost the opposite question: What should a robot do when falling becomes unavoidable? For humans, falling is a normal part of learning to move. Children fall repeatedly before they can walk confidently. Our bodies also react automatically when we lose balance. We change our posture, move our arms, and try to protect important parts of…
classificationReason: Entirely focused on humanoid robot fall dynamics, damage reduction, control, simulation training, and sim-to-real limits.
qualityReason: A coherent, technically developed explanatory episode covering physics, hardware, control, and experimentation.
